name: CASHBACK SBI Card

reward_terms.snapshot_note: CASHBACK SBI Card e-kit T&C, 47pp. Section 11 (Card Cashback) and Section 13 (fuel surcharge) are the ingested reward source.

version._note: Fee 999/999, renewal waived on annual spend >= 2,00,000 (see waiver threshold). Forex 3.5% (MITC standard, non-premium tier).

routes._note: Ratio 1.0 (direct rupee credit, no conversion) -- reward_terms Sec 11.1(a): 'Card Cashback earned on such SBI Card is directly credited to the SBI Card account within two working days of the statement generation.' route_type=statement_credit -- reward_terms FAQ 14: 'The Card Cashback will be automatically credited to your SBI Card account and will reflect in your monthly statement.'

currencies._note: Direct statement-credit cashback, v = 1, no redemption ambiguity -- resolved per _review_findings.checklist_item_7_currency_route_provenance (was FLAGGED by `ingest lint`, see docs/DECISIONS.md #129/#137). Key renamed from 'cashback_inr' to 'sbi_cashback_inr' on 2026-08-31 (docs/DECISIONS.md #139) -- the original key collided with the SYNTHETIC test catalog's own reward_currencies row of the same name (reward_currencies.key is globally unique in the schema, confirmed live), which `ingest link` correctly refused to let this real card silently share.

earning_rules._note: 5% on online spends. 'Online' identified by network online indicators (T&C 11.1.c). Floor rounding per txn (T&C 11.1.v: 2999 x 5% = 149, floored from 149.95).
1% on offline (non-online) spends. Any txn not flagged online is offline.

caps._note: Max 2,000 cashback on online per statement cycle. Overflow earns nothing (T&C 11: 'will not accrue any cashback till next cycle'). Statement-cycle approximated as calendar month (MVP; trace-flag cycle_approximated).
Max 2,000 cashback on offline per statement cycle.
Aggregate online+offline cashback capped 4,000 per statement cycle. Card-scoped so it binds across both earning rules.

exclusions._note: No cashback on: fuel, wallet, rent, jewelry, education, utility, insurance, card/gift/novelty, railways, member-FI/quasi-cash, digital gaming, tolls, government. MCC list per T&C 11.1.d table. These still count toward fee-waiver spend (not excluded from fee_waiver scope).

Cashback not applicable on transactions less than 100 (T&C 11.1.s). Modelled as exclusion of sub-100 txns from rewards. NOTE: category-mode approximation cannot see individual txns; flag as txn-mode-only precision.

_engine_compatibility_note: UPDATED as of Phase 5 Task A (docs/DECISIONS.md #130): both entries in exclusions[] above use selector fields (mcc_include, txn_max) that Part C defines -- these are now ENGINE-SUPPORTED. mcc_include is evaluated via a registry category->MCC map (engine.normalise.DEFAULT_CATEGORY_MCC_MAP, itself transcribed from this bundle's own sourced MCC table -- see that map's own comment) and flagged mcc_category_estimated; txn_max is accepted but deliberately unenforced in category mode (no per-transaction data to test it against) and flagged txn_threshold_unenforced instead of silently approximating. Loading exclusions[] as-is through bundle_from_dict is now safe -- the historical danger this note used to describe (_exclusion_selector_from_dict silently dropping these fields, producing an all-None ExclusionSelector that matched EVERYTHING and zeroed ALL cashback) is fixed; goldens/golden_mcc_gate_standalone.json is that fix's regression gate. tests/test_golden_sbi_cashback.py's _adapt_ingestion_bundle still drops exclusions[] for its own scenarios, but only because neither touches an MCC-excluded category or a sub-Rs100 ticket (provably inert either way), not because loading it is unsafe.

thresholds._note: Renewal fee waived on annual spend >= 2,00,000. Waiver-eligible spend = all spend, including rent/fuel (excluded from REWARDS but not from the waiver threshold).
thresholds._reviewer_note: Approved by Satya 2026-08-15: MITC p.4's waiver clause ('Waived off on annual spends of Rs.2 Lakh or more') carries no exclusion anywhere in the MITC, unlike the reward-side MCC exclusions which live in a separately-scoped section of the T&C -- all spend, including rent/fuel, counts toward the Rs.2L threshold. This approval covers the rent-inclusion reading specifically, not every fact citing 'mitc' as a source -- see _sources.mitc.reviewer_status (still 'unreviewed') and the still-open Rs.99 Rewards Redemption Fee question in _review_checklist.

surcharges._note: 1% fuel surcharge waiver on txns 500-3000, max 100/statement/account (FAQ 17 + T&C 13.1). UPDATED as of Phase 5 Task B (docs/DECISIONS.md #131/#132): the 'waiver' sub-object above IS now consumed, via engine.costs.Surcharge.waiver / SurchargeWaiver -- NOT as a separate earning_rule (the syn_fuel precedent, docs/DECISIONS.md #26, was tried first and confirmed empirically inert for this card: cashback_mcc_exclusions already strips ALL fuel spend from Stage 2's 'rewards' view, so a refund-shaped earning_rule can only ever see zero fuel segments). Computed instead directly in costs.surcharge_cost() against the same raw matched spend the surcharge itself uses, capped per statement_cycle instance, txn_min/txn_max accepted-but-unenforced-and-flagged same as Task A's posture. Verified: Rs8,000/month fuel spend nets to Rs0 surcharge cost (waived_base=Rs80 < Rs100 cap); Rs20,000/month nets to Rs118.00/month (capped at Rs100 pre-GST). See docs/DECISIONS.md #110 for the original gap this closes.

checklist_item_6_rs99_redemption_fee.verdict: APPROVED by Satya 2026-08-15: does NOT apply to CASHBACK
quotes: mitc p.31: "Rewards Redemption Fee: Rs.99. Applicable only on Physical products, Statement Credit & on Vouchers that are sent physically AS SPECIFIED IN THE INDIVIDUAL PRODUCT TERMS & CONDITIONS, for all cards except AURUM."
reward_terms FAQ 14: "What do I have to do to receive the earned Cashback? Ans: The Card Cashback will be automatically credited to your SBI Card account and will reflect in your monthly statement."
checklist_item_6_rs99_redemption_fee.reasoning: Three converging points, not one direct quote: (1) the MITC's own fee entry explicitly defers to 'the individual product Terms & Conditions' for applicability -- i.e. it points AT reward_terms Sec 11 to settle this, not at itself. (2) Sec 11 is unusually thorough (forfeiture events, timing, caps, minimum-txn threshold, rounding) yet never once mentions this fee, despite being exactly the kind of clause it would state if it applied. (3) FAQ 14 directly answers 'what do I have to do to receive cashback' with 'nothing -- automatic' -- a REDEMPTION fee presupposes an active redemption choice (typically: converting points into one of several catalog options -- merchandise, voucher, or statement credit), which CASHBACK's mechanism doesn't have at all; there is no catalog, no choice, nothing to redeem FROM. Sec 11.5(f) does use 'redeemed' once, for the narrow voluntary-closure edge case, but attaches no fee to it either. Net: the Rs.99 fee reads as aimed at SBI's POINTS-based cards (which the same MITC page separately notes have a 24-month Reward Point expiry and a redemption catalog), not at CASHBACK's direct percentage rebate. This was an absence-plus-context inference, not a single sentence saying 'CASHBACK is exempt' -- Claude proposed it, Satya reviewed and approved. No entity in this bundle models this fee (correctly, since it doesn't apply) -- the approval is recorded here rather than on a bundle field, since there's no field to attach it to.

quotes: reward_terms Sec 11.1(a): "Card Cashback earned on such SBI Card is directly credited to the SBI Card account within two working days of the statement generation."
reward_terms FAQ 12 (worked example): "An online transaction posted on 10th June of `40,000 would be eligible for a Card Cashback of 5% i.e. `2,000 ..."
reward_terms FAQ 14: "The Card Cashback will be automatically credited to your SBI Card account and will reflect in your monthly statement."
checklist_item_7_currency_route_provenan.reasoning: Sec 11.1(a)'s 'directly credited to the SBI Card account' establishes the statement_credit route_type (no redemption catalog, no separate claim step -- matches FAQ 14's 'will reflect in your monthly statement'). FAQ 12's worked example computes cashback as a straight percentage of a rupee spend amount, yielding a rupee cashback figure with no unit conversion anywhere -- establishes ratio=1.0. Corroborating absence-of-evidence: the ONLY 'reward points' mention anywhere in Section 11 (11.1(n)) is explicitly about a DIFFERENT SBI card variant a cardholder might be flipping FROM ('reward points accrued... on such variant would expire... prior to transferring... to CASHBACK SBI Card') -- CASHBACK's own mechanism is never described in points terms anywhere in the 47pp document, consistent with v=1 direct-rupee cashback, not a redemption-rate currency.
checklist_item_7_currency_route_provenan.source: reward_terms, Sec 11.1(a) + FAQ 12 + FAQ 14 -- both currencies[0] and currencies[0].routes[0] now carry _source: "reward_terms"
